edge.title: Add NorMuon row/col second-moment normalization after NS (NorMuonH)
edge.summary: Between Newton–Schulz and the hyperball step, NorMuonH divides the orthogonalized update by the square root of an EMA (beta2 0.95, clamp 1e-10) of its mean square over the short axis — one statistic per row for q/k/v, attn.proj and mlp.fc, and per column for the wide mlp.proj. This equalizes update magnitude across rows (columns), while the hyperball step still fixes the overall step at lr·‖W‖_F, so NorMuon's usual Frobenius re-scaling and any bias correction are unnecessary. Everything else is MuonH (#5); the schedule is shortened to 3275 steps and the record is claimed at the step-3250 validation, 25 steps before the LR reaches 0.

changes.label: Short-axis second-moment normalization
changes.detail: normuon_update: after NS and the aspect-ratio scale, v_new = mean(update²) over the last dim if rows ≥ cols (v shape [rows,1]) else over rows ([1,cols]); v.lerp_(v_new, 1 − 0.95); update ← update·rsqrt(max(v, 1e-10)). v is an fp32 zero-initialized per-matrix buffer, no bias correction.

changes.label: Schedule 3325→3275, claim at 3250
changes.detail: train_steps = 3275 sets the linear schedules; the reported val loss is the step-3250 eval (26·125), when the hidden lr multiplier is ≈0.008 and aux ≈0.02.

changes.label: Renames and docstrings
changes.detail: MuonH → NorMuonH and muon_update → normuon_update with updated docstrings; the hyperball helper, init, per-shape optimizer split, lr 0.018 and aux AdamW are untouched.

edge.parent_check: consistent — nearest code is #5 (70 changed lines), all in the optimizer and train_steps.
edge.noise: Renamed optimizer/update function and docstrings; hyperball helper, init, per-shape split and schedule code are unchanged.

mechanisms.name: NorMuon second-moment normalization
mechanisms.explain: normuon_update squares the orthogonalized update, averages it over the short axis, and keeps an fp32 EMA v (beta2 0.95) with one entry per row (or per column for the wide mlp.proj); the update is multiplied by rsqrt(max(v, 1e-10)). NS output has orthonormal columns for tall and orthonormal rows for wide matrices, so magnitudes vary along the long axis — exactly the axis this per-row/per-column EMA equalizes. Under the hyperball step only the resulting direction matters, so no Frobenius re-scaling or bias correction is applied.

mechanisms.name: Early stop before schedule end
mechanisms.explain: train_steps = 3275 defines the linear schedules, but the claimed result is the validation at step 3250 (a multiple of the 125-step eval interval), 25 steps before the LR reaches 0. At that point the hidden lr multiplier is ≈0.008 and the aux one ≈0.02.

caveats: Mechanically this is the same short-axis variance normalization (EMA 0.95, rsqrt, rows for tall/square, columns for wide) as #9's 'NorMuon-lite' and #10's 'NorMuon'; those also restore the pre-normalization Frobenius norm, which the hyperball step makes redundant here. Tagged `normuon` because the record names and cites NorMuon.
